title: Data set sidecar (set/1)
description: `<file>.champollion.json` beside ANY data file (TSV, JSONL, JSON, text, a word list): who holds it, what it is for, and where its text may go. One format read by every tool (mt-eval, nmt-forge, the champollion CLI, the MCP server) — the steward sidecar, given a schema. A sidecar can only make a file STRICTER: it never loosens what a corpus envelope or a registry entry says. A sidecar written before set/1 (no `$schema`) is read as set/0 — the same fields, without the new ones — and stays valid. Unknown keys are refused; put your own notes under an `x-` key.

$schema.description: Which schema this sidecar follows. Absent on a sidecar written before set/1.

transmission.description: local-only = only a model on this machine may ever see the text; every tool refuses to send it anywhere. The only restriction value a sidecar sets.

role.description: What the file is for in the project. train = may be learned from; dev = tuning and model selection; test = the protected set scores are reported on; sealed = a test set no one outside its holders sees; input = text to translate (deployment: source only, nothing to score); resource = a dictionary, glossary or grammar the methods use.

kind.description: What the file holds: sentence pairs, one-language text, a word list or dictionary, grammar notes, or a terminology glossary.

pair.description: The direction the file's columns run (source → target), in the language cards' codes.

fields.description: Which column or JSON field holds which side, when the file does not use `source`/`target`.

terms.description: What the people who hold this data said about its use, recorded where every tool can read it.

training.description: not-allowed = no tool may train a model on this file (enforced by nmt-forge's training mix); allowed = it may be learned from.

owner.description: Who holds this data, in the holder's own words.

speakers.description: Whose words the file holds — the people who said or wrote them — in the holder's own words (a family chat or an elder's notebooks hold other people's words).

speakers_agreed.description: Whether the people whose words these are agreed to their use: yes; not-yet (not asked yet — no model may learn from it until they agree); some-said-no (no model may learn from this file — take their words out into another file first).

consent_record.description: Path (relative to this file's folder) of the consent note that records who agreed to what, and when.

id.description: The registered corpus id (written by `champollion network register-corpus`); read verbatim, never re-derived.

license.description: The licence the holder states (an SPDX id or a LicenseRef-*).

segment.description: The corpus segment, as in a JSON envelope (e.g. `held_out`).

sha256.description: SHA-256 of the data file when it was registered; a changed file no longer gets the card's id or grade.

card.description: Path (relative to this file's folder) of the corpora card registered for it.

derived_from.description: The protected file this one was derived from (a split, a cleaned copy, a run's outputs); its marks were carried here.

holders_agreed.description: Who among the data's holders agreed that this file — the output of a method whose output is local-only — could be written where it is, outside its project, and when (written by `mt-eval translate --holders-agreed-by`). It loosens nothing: the file stays local-only for every tool.

by.description: Who agreed, as they were named.

written_by.description: The tool command that wrote this sidecar.
